ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Post-pause palpitation

A 38-year-old notices a forceful thump after an isolated ventricular premature beat. Monitoring shows that the premature contraction produces a weak peripheral pulse, then a pause before a strong sinus beat. What best explains the especially noticeable subsequent beat?

  1. Complete failure of atrial contraction throughout the pause
  2. Persistent ventricular fibrillation
  3. Sudden anatomic closure of the aortic valve
  4. A new complete AV block after every PVC
  5. Greater filling and post-extrasystolic potentiation
Answer and explanation

Greater filling and post-extrasystolic potentiation

The pause permits filling and the next contraction may be stronger, producing the perceived thump.

Option explanations

Greater filling and post-extrasystolic potentiation: The pause permits filling and the next contraction may be stronger, producing the perceived thump.

Complete failure of atrial contraction throughout the pause: Atrial activity may continue and does not explain the stronger contraction by itself.

Persistent ventricular fibrillation: Ventricular fibrillation would not yield stable subsequent sinus beats.

Sudden anatomic closure of the aortic valve: Normal valve closure cannot explain the consistent post-ectopic pattern.

A new complete AV block after every PVC: A recurring PVC does not establish complete AV block.
